historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment anchored on the 3-yr revenue CAGR (5.2%) and FY2027 guidance (7.25-7.75% organic, which includes ~1.7pp from the 53rd week and the faster-growing Diabetes unit being removed); equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because dividends ($3.6bn) plus buybacks exceed retained earnings every year, so book value shrinks while the business grows.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.6% 5-yr, -1.0% 3-yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (3.8%/5.2%) and EPS (7.0%/9.8%): the payout ratio exceeds 100% of GAAP earnings after buybacks, so book value is not a growth signal for Medtronic.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY26 5,426-457-383 = 4,586; FY23 4,580-355-394 = 3,831 (interest income FY23 = 9M 246 + Q4 148); FY21 4,885-344-~150 = ~4,391 (FY21 interest income not in the DB; ~150 assumed for a near-zero-rate year, so the 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR is approximate). Owner FCF 3-yr CAGR 6.2% vs reported 5.8%: SBC grew 9%/yr (355 -> 457) but interest income fell 394 -> 383, so the two adjustments roughly offset; SBC is only 1.3% of revenue and is not the story here. The 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR (~0.9%) is depressed by FY21 being a strong post-COVID working-capital release year and FY26 carrying separation cash costs. Historical FCF margins: 13.0% FY24, 12.7% FY25, 12.6% FY26 on an owner basis. Metrics.csv period labels for quarters are two fiscal quarters out (the XBRL fp tag mislabel: the 'Q3 2026' row with revenue 9,756 is Q1 FY2027, the 'Q1 2026' row 9,017 is Q3 FY2026); annual rows are correct.

scenario_narratives.base: Continuing Medtronic (Cardiovascular, Neuroscience, Medical Surgical) grows ~5% underlying through FY29 as Cardiac Ablation Solutions keeps compounding on Affera/Sphere-9/Sphere-360 (88% growth in Q1 FY27, still gaining share against Boston Scientific's FARAPULSE and J&J), Hugo ramps slowly in US urology then general surgery without denting Intuitive, and renal denervation reimbursement builds; CRM and spine grow mid-single digits, China VBP headwinds are 'mostly behind'. The pre-SBC EBITDA margin absorbs the ~$250m tariff headwind in FY27 and then expands ~30bp/yr toward 29.5% from mix and the removal of the loss-making Diabetes unit and its stranded costs. Cash taxes fall from 28% to 25% of EBIT as transition-tax instalments end. Growth fades to 2.5% by year 10 and the terminal value is capped at 18x owner FCF (Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be 20.5x).
scenario_narratives.bull: PFA becomes a three-player market in which Medtronic holds ~30% share and CAS exceeds $2bn by FY29; Hugo gains general-surgery and gynaecology indications and wins second-system placements at cost-sensitive hospitals; Symplicity renal denervation gets broad CMS coverage; the December 2026 Investor Day sets a 6%+ organic algorithm and the market re-rates Medtronic toward Boston Scientific. Margins expand 50bp/yr to 31% (mix plus TSA-funded stranded-cost removal), cash tax settles at 23% after the IRS matters close, and the 15% Investor-Day-style capital return (buybacks funded by the exchange-offer share retirement) keeps the count flat without extra cash. Terminal growth 2.75%, still capped at 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY27 acceleration proves to be comps and the 53rd week: Boston Scientific and J&J hold PFA share with second-generation catheters, Hugo stalls at niche placements while absorbing R&D and fleet capex, a renewed China VBP round hits neurovascular and spine, and tariffs escalate beyond $250m. Stranded Diabetes costs are not removed and TSA income rolls off, holding the pre-SBC EBITDA margin at ~26.5%; cash taxes stay at 28-30% of EBIT with Pillar Two and the IRS dispute; working capital keeps consuming 30% of each revenue dollar. Growth settles at 2% and a cyclically-sensitive terminal multiple of 15x applies. Balance-sheet risk is not part of the bear case: $28bn of A-rated debt against ~$10bn EBITDA is comfortably serviced.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Pro-forma continuing-operations owner-FCF DCF on a 10-year component build: the Diabetes unit (8.6% of revenue, ~3% operating margin) is stripped from the flows and the retained MiniMed stake is carried at market in the equity bridge pending the split-off exchange. Owner FCF is reported FCF less SBC and less the interest earned on the $7.1bn investment portfolio that is netted against debt. Cash taxes are modelled at the actual cash rate on EBIT (28% ramping to 25%), not the 17% non-GAAP rate; working capital is charged as a cash consumer. The share count is held flat because SBC is fully expensed; buybacks are value-neutral. The terminal value is capped at 18x year-10 owner FCF (15x bear).
key_risks_to_valuation: Exchange-offer mechanics: the MiniMed stake is valued at the MMED market price; if MMED trades materially lower before completion, or the offer is undersubscribed and Medtronic retains a stake it must dispose of later, the ~$3.9/share bridge item shrinks. The item is first-order neutral to completion itself.
Stranded cost and TSA roll-off after the separation are not disclosed; the model assumes ~$150m stranded cost removed over two years. The December 2026 Investor Day should quantify this.

Cash tax rate: the model charges 28% falling to 25% on EBIT. If cash taxes revert toward the ~21% GAAP provision rate the valuation is ~8% too low; if the IRS transfer-pricing dispute resolves adversely, cash taxes could exceed 30% for several years.
Terminal value is ~55-60% of enterprise value; the 18x cap binds in base and bull, so the value is not sensitive to terminal growth but is to the cap choice.
Tariffs (~$250m FY27 pre-tax, policy-dependent) and China VBP are modelled as a one-year margin step; escalation would compound through the margin path.
Working-capital drag has been 1.5-3.9% of revenue; the model charges ~0.6% of year-1 revenue. If separation-related outflows do not fade, year-1 FCF is overstated by ~$400-600m.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 73.31-106.33. MMED (MiniMed) close from the same endpoint, same timestamp.
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR: FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-06-18, accession 0001628280-26-044354) for segment revenue/profit, interest income, D&A split, cash flow; Q1 FY2027 10-Q (filed 2026-09-03, 0001628280-26-060473) for the 31 Jul 2026 balance sheet, diluted shares, Diabetes quarter; Q1 FY2027 earnings release 8-K Ex-99.1 (2026-09-01) for guidance and the 53rd-week estimate; SC TO-I/A (2026-09-17) for exchange-offer share counts; MiniMed Group 10-Q (CIK 0002062583, filed 2026-09-08) for MiniMed cash, debt and share count. inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 (52 weeks to 24 Apr 2026) consolidated net sales 36,364 less Diabetes 3,112 = 33,252 pro forma continuing (Cardiovascular 13,976 + Neuroscience 10,287 + Medical Surgical 8,815 + other 135 + Italian payback adj 39). FY2026 10-K segment note.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average, Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 31 Jul 2026): 1,285.1m diluted vs 1,279.8m basic; 1,280.0m basic issued at 31 Jul 2026. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks (FY26 $1,035m, Q1 FY27 $267m) fund the flat count. NOT yet reduced for the MiniMed split-off exchange offer (open at valuation date; see equity_bridge) -- when it closes, cut the count by the Medtronic shares accepted and delete the MiniMed bridge item.
inputs.cash_basis: 31 Jul 2026: cash 1,691 + short-term investments (marketable debt securities, 'global liquidity structures') 7,128 = 8,819, less MiniMed's own cash 207 (MiniMed 10-Q, 31 Jul 2026; MiniMed has no debt drawn) = 8,612. Total debt = current 2,536 + long-term 25,617 = 28,153 (no MiniMed debt inside it). Net debt 19,541 is therefore ex-MiniMed.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, stock-based compensation add-back $457m. Medtronic does not disclose cash paid for share withholding on award vesting as a separate line ('Issuance of shares under stock purchase and award plans, net of shares withheld for taxes' is netted in the equity statement), so the cash-flow add-back is used as the combined figure. Interest income $383m (FY26; $511m FY25, $597m FY24) from the investments note -- stripped because the $7.1bn investment portfolio is netted against debt in net_debt.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: last Friday of April (FY2026 ended 24 Apr 2026; FY2027 is a 53-week year ending 30 Apr 2027, extra week in Q1)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10-year UST ~4.1%, ERP 4.5%, beta ~0.75 (low-beta, non-discretionary medtech) -> cost of equity ~7.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (A-rated senior notes; FY26 net interest expense $715m on ~$28bn), ~3.6% after tax. Debt ~20% of EV-weighted capital -> ~6.7%; rounded UP to 7.0% to carry separation execution and tariff/China policy risk in the rate rather than in an ad-hoc premium. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the probability weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (liability $1,188m at 24 Apr 2026, cash payments $270m FY26) are expensed inside operating income and therefore already inside the EBITDA margin path; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Finance leases immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% of the continuing (ex-Diabetes) segments, which are essentially wholly owned. Noncontrolling interests of $618m at 31 Jul 2026 split into ~$357m MiniMed public float (10.1% of MiniMed book equity $3,532m) -- handled by valuing the MiniMed stake at market in the bridge, not by the flows -- and ~$260m other NCI, deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, medtech). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FRAMING: pro-forma continuing operations ex-Diabetes. Medtronic is split-off-ing MiniMed (MMED, IPO'd Mar-2026 at $20, Medtronic retains 252.8m of 281.2m shares = 89.9%) via an exchange offer launched 14 Sep 2026 (SC TO-I) for up to 225.4m MMED shares (80.1%) plus a 27.5m de-minimis top-up; the offer was still open at the valuation date (daily 425 filings through 1 Oct 2026, no results 8-K). FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 statements still consolidate Diabetes, so the flows are rebuilt ex-Diabetes from the segment note: FY26 continuing revenue 33,252 (Diabetes 3,112 removed); reportable-segment operating profit 8,862 (26.8% of 33,079) vs Diabetes+other operating segments profit of only 106 after corporate/SBC allocations, i.e. Diabetes was ~3% margin and its removal LIFTS the continuing margin ~2pp while cutting revenue 8.6%. Pro-forma FY26 EBITDA before SBC: consolidated GAAP operating income 6,467 + D&A 2,958 + SBC 457 = 9,882, less Diabetes EBITDA ~200, less ~150 stranded corporate cost assumed to persist 2 years = ~9,530 = 28.7% of 33,252; this basis INCLUDES recurring restructuring (249-389/yr), litigation (113-317/yr), acquisition-related items and currency/hedging within other operating expense, which are charged as recurring costs, not added back. The MiniMed stake is carried in equity_bridge at the MMED market price; the exchange retires Medtronic shares for MMED shares at approximately market value (standard ~7% tender discount transfers a small amount from non-tendering to tendering holders), so per-share value is first-order neutral to completion. UPDATE RULE: once the exchange closes, (1) delete the MiniMed bridge item, (2) set shares_outstanding to the post-exchange diluted count, (3) remove the stranded-cost drag per management disclosure at the Dec-2026 Investor Day. CASH TAX: modelled on EBIT after full D&A (amortisation 1,772 in FY26); cash taxes paid were 30.0% of GAAP EBIT in FY26 (1,942/6,467), 30.5% FY25, 31.5% FY24, versus a 21.2% GAAP provision rate and 17.3% non-GAAP rate -- cash exceeds provision because of IRS disputes, DTL unwind and transition-tax instalments (final instalment FY26). Base ramps 28% -> 25% as instalments end; bear holds 30%. WORKING CAPITAL: Medtronic is a manufacturer (receivables + inventory > payables) and 'other operating assets and liabilities' has been a persistent outflow (-865 FY26, -538 FY25, -345 FY24; inventories -404/-292/-139; receivables -200/-433/-391), a total drag of 3.9%/3.1%/1.5% of revenue, inflated in FY26 by separation and litigation cash costs. wc_capture is therefore NEGATIVE (-25% of the revenue increase in base) -- growth consumes cash. 53RD WEEK: FY2027 has 14 weeks in Q1 (~$570m, ~1.7% of annual revenue); year-1 growth includes it and year-2 growth laps it. TARIFF: management's ~$250m pre-tax FY27 net headwind (~0.75% of revenue) is absorbed in the year-1 margin step-down from 28.7% pro forma to 28.0%. SANITY: year-1 base owner FCF ~5.3bn on 35.6bn revenue (14.8%) vs FY26 consolidated owner FCF 4,586 (12.6%, depressed by the 3.9% WC/other drag and Diabetes) and Q1 FY27 reported FCF 1,290 (vs 584 PY).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (FY27) = ~5.3% underlying continuing-portfolio growth (guidance 7.25-7.75% organic for the whole company incl. 53rd week and 15%-growing Diabetes) + ~1.7pp 53rd week. Y2 laps the extra week. Y3-Y5 4.5-5%: PFA (Affera/Sphere-9/Sphere-360) continuing to take share, Hugo US ramp, renal denervation, CRM mid-single-digit; fade to 2.5% by Y9-10 as PFA matures.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA after recurring restructuring/litigation/currency charges. Pro-forma FY26 continuing = 28.7%; Y1 steps down to 28.0% for the ~$250m tariff headwind and stranded corporate cost, then +30bp/yr to 29.5% (mix shift to CAS/PFA, Hugo scale, stranded cost removal) -- consistent with management's historical 50bp/yr non-GAAP operating-margin expansion target, haircut.
base.da_rationale: FY26 D&A 2,958 = 8.1% consolidated (depreciation 1,186 + amortisation 1,772); ex-Diabetes ~8.4%. Covidien-era (2015) intangibles roll off through ~FY30, so the amortisation tax shield shrinks toward depreciation (~3.3%) plus bolt-on amortisation (~1.7%). D&A only affects the cash-tax base in this engine; it is added back in full.
base.capex_rationale: FY26 capex 1,904 = 5.2% consolidated (4.9% FY24, 5.5% FY25). Includes Hugo system placements and manufacturing capacity; eases to 4.8% as the Hugo fleet build matures.
base.cash_tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid / GAAP EBIT: 30.0% FY26, 30.5% FY25, 31.5% FY24 (vs 21% provision; IRS disputes, DTL unwind, transition-tax instalments ending FY26). Ramps to 25% as the instalments and Italian payback cash-outs roll off; Pillar Two (15% minimum) stops the rate going back toward the 17% non-GAAP rate.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables + inventory grow with sales and 'other operating assets and liabilities' is a persistent outflow (-865/-538/-345 FY26/25/24). -25% of the revenue increase charges ~0.6% of Y1 revenue, well below the 1.5-3.9% historical drag, which carried separation and litigation cash costs that are expected to fade.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%: the thesis rests on the FY27 re-acceleration being durable rather than a 53rd-week/comps artefact, and three live external risks (tariffs, China VBP, PFA share war) are outside management's control; no solvency or covenant element, so not higher. Bull cut to 30% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (PFA share hold, Hugo adoption against Intuitive's installed base, RDN reimbursement, and the Investor Day re-rating). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
